purpose: Check whether the trial-wise normalisation that helped the fixed centroid probe (experiment 76) also helps a learnable MLP readout, or whether it only compensates for the weak probe.

data.eeg: public train only, 50 ms log1p counts

arms.base: per-session z-score, fitted on the three training repeats
arms.trial_z: base, then each trial z-scored across its own features

readout.model: src.neural.SpikeClassifier, 2748 classes, hidden 1024, dropout 0, apply_log False
readout.training: AdamW lr 3e-4, weight decay 0, batch 256, gradient clip 5, seed 42, fixed 10 epochs
readout.note: identical for both arms and identical to the experiment-74 base, so any difference is due to the input transform

metrics.top1: held argmax identity accuracy over 10992 held rows per mouse-fold
metrics.recall32: held character inside the top-32 logits
metrics.recall100: held character inside the top-100 logits
metrics.ocf: official OCF, fold k=4 only, Hungarian over each 2748-trial session block, RNG123 heldout pictures [256:768]

pass_rule.advance: trial_z improves recall32 over base for BOTH mice in at least 3 of 4 folds each AND fold-4 OCF improves for both mice
pass_rule.reject: otherwise the transform only compensates for the centroid probe and is not adopted

prohibited: changing epochs, hidden size, or seed between arms
selecting on the held repeat or on heldout pictures
